items.title: Duran Duran's original guitarist Andy Taylor dies aged 65
items.why: Andy Taylor, whose guitar shaped 1980s hits such as Rio and Girls on Film, died of prostate cancer at home on Monday, his family and the band said on Wednesday. The band has sold more than 100 million records.

items.title: Fuel truck fire kills at least 31 on highway in Greater Cairo
items.why: A truck carrying petroleum products overturned and caught fire on the Ring Road in Warraq, Giza, part of Greater Cairo, on Wednesday, burning 27 vehicles. Egypt's health ministry says at least 31 people died and 21 were injured. Prosecutors have opened an investigation.

items.title: US proposes new tariffs on China, the EU and 12 other economies
items.why: The US trade office on Wednesday proposed import taxes of mostly 10% to 20% on 14 economies, including China, the EU, India and Japan, saying they produce far more than they need. China would face 20%. The duties would not start before public hearings in January.
items.matters: Tariffs can raise prices for shoppers and hurt exporters; China calls the claims false and the EU rejects them.

items.title: US Army blows up unstable lead explosives at Iowa plant
items.why: The US Army detonated about five tons of degraded lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown on Wednesday, saying it risked exploding on its own. Environmental groups had sued over fears of toxic lead dust. Federal agencies say early air tests found no detectable lead.
items.matters: Lead is harmful at any level and especially dangerous to children and pregnant women.

items.title: Storm forces first weather postponement of New York's Thanksgiving parade
items.why: Macy's has moved its 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York from Thursday to Saturday as a powerful storm brings heavy rain, coastal flooding and strong winds to the US East Coast. Forecasters warn of gusts of around 60 mph in the city.
items.matters: More than 81 million Americans are expected to travel this week, so delays and power cuts are likely.
items.changed: Updated: New York's Thanksgiving parade was moved to Saturday

items.title: London Museum prepares to open in old Smithfield meat market
items.why: The free London Museum, about the history of the British capital, opens in its new home in the Victorian buildings of Smithfield Market on Saturday 28 November. The move cost £437 million, up from a 2019 budget of £337 million.
items.matters: The museum hopes to draw more than two million visitors a year.

items.title: At least nine dead as rescuers search flooded Indonesian gold mine
items.why: Rescuers had recovered nine bodies by Wednesday from an unlicensed gold mine in Bogor regency, West Java, which flooded late on Monday, AP reports; the state news agency Antara reported 13 on Thursday. About 17 miners are still believed trapped, and 11 escaped.
items.changed: Updated: more bodies have been recovered

items.title: Asian stock markets fall sharply as doubts over AI boom return
items.why: Chipmakers led steep falls across Asia on Wednesday. Taiwan's and South Korea's main indexes dropped around 5 to 6%, and Japan's Nikkei more than 3%. Samsung, SK Hynix and TSMC each fell around 8 to 9%, after Nvidia shares dropped almost 6% in New York on Tuesday.
items.matters: Many pension and savings funds hold these big tech shares, so falls can affect ordinary savers.

items.title: North Korea expels Swiss envoy over sanctions on children's camp
items.why: North Korea has told Sylvain Astier, head of Switzerland's office in Pyongyang, to leave within 48 hours and the office to close, state media said on Wednesday. It objects to Swiss sanctions on a camp in Wonsan that Switzerland says has hosted Ukrainian children taken from Russian-occupied areas.
items.matters: Switzerland reopened the office only in October, as one of few Western contacts with North Korea.

items.title: Australia's inflation rises to 4.9%, its highest in three years
items.why: Consumer prices in Australia rose 4.9% in the year to October, up from 4.3% in September and above forecasts, the Australian Bureau of Statistics said on Wednesday. Fuel prices rose 32.5% and electricity 25.2%. Treasurer Jim Chalmers blamed a spike in global oil prices.
items.matters: High inflation makes an interest rate cut by Australia's central bank less likely.

items.title: Kilmar Abrego Garcia leaves the US for Spain after deportation fight
items.why: Kilmar Abrego Garcia, a Salvadoran man wrongly deported to El Salvador in 2025 and later returned, flew from Washington to Madrid on Tuesday. The Homeland Security secretary says he 'self-deported'; his lawyer says he left on his own terms rather than be sent to Liberia.

items.title: US jury convicts Huawei of conspiring to steal trade secrets
items.why: A federal jury in New York on Tuesday found China's Huawei guilty on 10 of 12 counts, including conspiracy to steal trade secrets and bank fraud, after a three-month trial. It was cleared of racketeering conspiracy and obstruction of justice. Huawei says the convictions are 'without legal or factual merit'.
items.matters: Huawei is one of the world's biggest telecoms firms, and the verdict adds to tension between the US and China.
items.changed: Updated: Huawei responded to the verdict

items.title: Ukraine defends drone strike on Russian ships in Libya's Benghazi
items.why: Ukraine's foreign minister, Andrii Sybiha, called weekend drone strikes on a Russian warship and a cargo ship at Benghazi, in eastern Libya, legitimate self-defence. Libya's Tripoli-based government condemned the attack. Eastern Libyan authorities say two of their navy soldiers died of wounds from it.
items.matters: It carries the war in Ukraine to Africa, in a country split between rival governments.

items.title: Colombian forces free hostages held in Cartagena supermarket
items.why: Police and troops stormed an Éxito supermarket in Cartagena, Colombia, at about 1:30am on Wednesday, ending a siege of more than 17 hours. President Abelardo de la Espriella says all the hostages were freed and one gunman was killed. Infobae reports four suspects were captured.
items.changed: Updated: security forces ended the siege and freed the hostages

items.title: Jannik Sinner has knee surgery and may miss the Australian Open
items.why: Italy's Jannik Sinner, the world number two, said on Tuesday he had surgery on his right knee in Turku, Finland. He has not played since winning Wimbledon in July. One specialist says he could be out for three to four months; the Australian Open starts on 17 January.

items.title: Music streaming service Tidal to remove songs made entirely by AI
items.why: Tidal said on Tuesday that from 9 December it will reject and remove tracks made wholly by artificial intelligence, though songs made with AI help are still allowed. It says 43% of tracks sent to it in the past 90 days were fully AI-generated.
items.matters: CBC says Tidal is the first major streaming service to ban fully AI-generated music.

items.title: Sport court gives Senegal back its Africa Cup of Nations title
items.why: The Court of Arbitration for Sport on Tuesday unanimously restored Senegal's 1-0 extra-time win over Morocco in January's final. African football's governing body, CAF, had awarded Morocco the title in March because Senegal's players walked off in protest. Morocco's federation says it will pursue legal options.

items.title: Houthis say they hit Saudi ports as missiles intercepted over Riyadh
items.why: Yemen's Houthis say they attacked the Saudi ports of Jeddah and Jazan on Wednesday after coalition strikes on Hodeidah. The Saudi-led coalition says a projectile caused minor damage at Jazan, with no injuries, and that it later shot down two ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh.
items.matters: Ras Tanura handles about 16% of Saudi refining capacity, so attacks there can push up oil prices worldwide.
items.changed: Updated: the Houthis say they targeted two Saudi ports; missiles were intercepted over Riyadh

items.title: Putin says Russia will retaliate for Ukrainian strikes on oil refineries
items.why: President Vladimir Putin said on Tuesday that Ukraine was ignoring President Trump's request to stop hitting Russian refineries, and that 'retaliatory measures on our part are inevitable'. Industry sources told Reuters the attacks have cut Russian refining by 45% since late October. Kyiv says it will stop if Moscow does.

items.title: Indian teenager Vaibhav Sooryavanshi hits record 204 off 53 balls
items.why: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, 15, scored 204 off 53 balls for India A against the UAE in Doha on Tuesday, setting 50-over (List A) records for the fastest hundred (28 balls) and double hundred (52 balls). He also hit a record 28 sixes as India won by seven wickets.

items.title: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill senior Hamas security official and six others
items.why: Israeli strikes in Gaza on Tuesday killed at least seven people, including Naeem Abu Nahel, head of Hamas's internal security service, according to Gaza's Hamas-run interior ministry and medics. Israel's military said it struck a senior militant. The strikes came despite the ceasefire agreed in October 2025.

items.title: China investigates Shanghai Communist Party chief Chen Jining
items.why: China's anti-corruption watchdog is investigating Chen Jining, Shanghai's Communist Party secretary and a Politburo member, for 'suspected severe violations of discipline and laws', state media said on Tuesday. The phrase usually means corruption. He is the fourth Politburo member investigated since 2025.
items.matters: Shanghai's party chief job is often a step to China's top leadership; Premier Li Qiang once held it.

items.title: UK warns firms supplying Ukraine of Russian sabotage threat
items.why: Britain's defence ministry and MI5's protective security arm warned companies supplying Ukraine's military on Tuesday that Russia has stepped up sabotage attempts against European defence sites, often using proxies and methods such as arson. Russia's embassy in London rejects any link to such activity.

items.title: Landmines killed or injured nearly 7,000 people in 2025, report says
items.why: At least 6,929 people were killed or injured by landmines and other explosive remnants of war in 2025, the highest total since 2020, says the Landmine Monitor 2026 report. Most were civilians. Myanmar (1,891) and Syria (1,602) recorded the most casualties.

items.title: UN says partners or relatives killed 47,000 women and girls in 2025
items.why: About 47,000 women and girls were killed by partners or family members in 2025, roughly five every hour, UN Women and the UN Office on Drugs and Crime said on Tuesday. That is 60% of about 78,000 women and girls killed intentionally. Africa had the highest rate.

items.title: China launches first space station mission with a foreign astronaut
items.why: A Long March-2F rocket lifted off from Jiuquan in north-west China at 00:18 GMT on Wednesday, carrying Shenzhou-24 to the Tiangong station. Its crew includes Pakistan Air Force pilot Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, 40, the first Pakistani in space and the first foreign astronaut on a Chinese mission.
items.matters: It is China's first crewed space mission to include an astronaut from another country.

items.title: Iraq's top court backs Baghdad's control of Kurdish borders and oil
items.why: Iraq's Federal Supreme Court ruled on Wednesday that federal forces can be deployed on all international borders, including in the Kurdish region, and that the Oil Ministry can oversee oil and gas fields. It came a day after Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi ordered a takeover of Kurdish-run crossings and oilfields.
items.matters: Control of oil and its income has long divided Baghdad and the Kurdish region; this could deepen the dispute.
items.changed: Updated: Iraq's top court backed the federal government's powers

items.title: Sanofi agrees to buy US drugmaker Insmed for about $41bn
items.why: French drugmaker Sanofi will pay $175 a share in cash for Insmed, maker of the lung disease drug Brinsupri, the companies said on Tuesday. It is the drug industry's biggest takeover since Pfizer bought Seagen in 2023. Sanofi's shares rose almost 11% in Paris.
items.matters: Big drug firms are buying new medicines as patents on their best-sellers run out.

items.title: Pope Francis's private diary, now published, describes seeing the devil
items.why: A book of the late Pope Francis's private notes from 1992 to 2024, edited by Cardinal Víctor Manuel Fernández, came out on Tuesday in five languages. In it Francis describes seeing the devil several times and a spiritual crisis in 2021 and 2022.

items.title: Silver coins looted from 1712 Dutch shipwreck returned to Australia
items.why: Twenty-three silver coins taken from the Zuytdorp, a Dutch East India Company ship wrecked off Western Australia in 1712, were handed back in Canberra on Tuesday. The FBI found 21 in California and Dutch police seized two in Amsterdam. They will go to a museum in Fremantle.

items.changed: Updated: the treaty was signed in Canberra
items.title: Australia and Solomon Islands sign treaty barring foreign military bases
items.why: Prime Ministers Anthony Albanese and Matthew Wale signed a treaty in Canberra on Wednesday. Solomon Islands will host no foreign military or security base and will consult Australia on security. ABC reports it will let its 2022 pact with China lapse; Wale cites a non-disclosure clause.
items.matters: The 2022 pact alarmed Australia and the US because it opened the way for Chinese forces in the South Pacific.

items.title: Bangladesh's ousted leader Sheikh Hasina says she will return on 16 December
items.why: Sheikh Hasina, Bangladesh's former prime minister, plans to return from exile in India on 16 December, her spokesman says, and has asked for a flight on the state airline. She was sentenced to death in her absence. A government minister says she can only return in handcuffs.

items.title: California braces for flooding as king tides meet strong El Niño
items.why: Exceptionally high 'king tides' peaking on Wednesday, a strong El Niño and record-warm seas could bring severe coastal flooding to California during Thanksgiving week, AFP reports. The US National Weather Service warns of up to nearly three feet (0.9m) of flooding around San Francisco Bay.
items.matters: San Francisco's mayor, Daniel Lurie, has urged people to limit unnecessary travel in the busiest US travel week.

items.title: Car bomb wounds at least 23 people in Colombian city of Villavicencio
items.why: A car bomb exploded on Monday night in Villavicencio, capital of Meta province in central Colombia, wounding at least 23 people and damaging buildings, according to reports. President Abelardo de la Espriella blamed a dissident faction of the former FARC rebels.

items.title: Australia passes law to fine tech giants up to 5% of revenue
items.why: Australia's parliament passed the digital duty of care law on Wednesday after Labor struck a deal with the Greens. Platforms that fail to protect users could be fined up to 5% of global revenue, and Australians will be able to sue them. The opposition Coalition voted against it.
items.matters: SBS estimates Meta alone could face fines of around A$10 billion; the US ambassador has objected to the law.
items.changed: Updated: the law has passed parliament

items.title: Ebola workers evacuated from Congo hospital after days of fighting
items.why: WHO staff and Congolese health officials who sheltered for over three days in a hospital in Akwe, Ituri province, have been evacuated, WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said on Tuesday. Fighting nearby has disrupted the Ebola response. The WHO counts 11,762 confirmed cases and 5,775 deaths.
items.matters: It is the largest and deadliest Ebola outbreak recorded in the country, and violence is making it harder to contain.
items.changed: Updated: the trapped health workers have been evacuated
Updated: 24 body bags recovered; about 30 to 34 people still missing
items.title: Indonesia factory fire: 24 body bags recovered and dozens still missing
items.why: Rescuers had recovered 24 body bags from a burned sweets factory in Cikande, Banten province, west of Jakarta, by Sunday evening, officials say. Remains must be identified by DNA, which could take weeks. About 30 to 34 people are still missing, according to differing official counts.
